title: Credibility assessment of explicit finite element models for guidewire core torque transmission under ASME V&V 40
runhead: V&V40 credibility for guidewire torque FEA
device: Steerable vascular guidewire core intended for percutaneous cardiovascular procedures

models.name: HF-Explicit-3D
models.what_it_computes: Three-dimensional explicit FEA of core, distal coil, and jacket with surface-to-surface contact to predict transient proximal-to-distal torque transmission, local torsional strain and stress, and energy dissipation under imposed proximal rotation.

models.name: MF-Explicit-Beam
models.what_it_computes: Reduced-order explicit FEA using homogenized beam and shell representations with nonlinear torsion and Coulomb friction to approximate distal rotational response and torque loss.

mechanisms.name: Elastic torsional transmission (wind-up)
mechanisms.why_it_matters: Determines rotational lag and fidelity of tip response during steering, directly affecting controllability and positioning accuracy.

mechanisms.name: Interfacial slip-driven torque loss
mechanisms.why_it_matters: Captures frictional slip between core and surrounding layers leading to torque attenuation and overshoot, impacting navigability and operator feedback.

clear_factors: Relevance of the quantities of interest

deviation.detail: All credibility factors are scored on a 0–12 Credibility Readiness Index (CRI), where higher values indicate stronger evidence.

context_of_use.statement: Use explicit finite element analyses to predict torque transmission metrics of guidewire core designs—specifically distal rotation per unit proximal rotation and torque loss—in benchtop analogs of tortuous coronary anatomy, to inform design selection and to reduce the scope of physical torque transmission testing prior to verification testing.
context_of_use.rationale: Model outputs are used to rank design variants and to screen out underperforming concepts before formal verification. Decisions supported by the model are confined to preverification design selection; bench verification tests are retained for final acceptance.

model_risk.rationale: Inaccurate predictions could lead to selecting a design with suboptimal torque control, increasing the probability of extended procedure time or device exchange. However, mitigations include mandatory physical verification tests prior to release and no direct patient-level decisions based solely on simulation.

scores.scale: 0–12 Credibility Readiness Index (CRI); higher indicates stronger evidence for credibility of that factor
